Maya (Support): Hey team, ACME reported a spike in API 500s and token latency on their private cluster (acme-reserved-3) starting ~2024-06-01T15:22Z. Example request-id: req_0a1b2c3d4e5f. They say curl repro sometimes gets 500 immediately. Can we collect a minimal repro bundle + node/gpu stats?

Sam (Oncall): Got it. Can you paste the exact request-id and the full curl they used? Also which model and region?

Maya (Support): Request-id above. Model: redwood/gpt-7b-v1, tenant: acme-corp, region: eu-west-1 (private VPC). Customer sent this curl:

```bash
curl -sS -X POST "https://api.redwood-inference.internal/v1/generate" \\n  -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" \\n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \\n  -d '{"model":"redwood/gpt-7b-v1","input":"summarize: long document","max_new_tokens":256}'
```

Maya (Support): They also said sometimes the request succeeds but latency jumps to 8-12s p95.

Jordan (Infra): Thanks. First steps: we need (1) pod logs for inference replicas, (2) kubelet/journal logs for the node that hosted the pod, (3) nvidia-smi and dmesg around the time of the errors, (4) container traces (if any) and the nginx/ingress logs. I'll list exact commands below clients can run if they have access, otherwise we can collect via control-plane.

Jordan (Infra): Commands to run on cluster control-plane (or we can run with support privileges):

```bash
# list pods for the tenant (namespace may be tenant-specific)
kubectl -n acme-corp get pods -l app=inference

# fetch logs for the inference container, include previous to capture crashes
kubectl -n acme-corp logs <pod-name> -c inference --tail=500 --since=2h > /tmp/acme_inference_logs.txt

# node-level logs (kubelet + systemd)
ssh core@<node-host> "sudo journalctl -u kubelet --since \"2024-06-01 14:30\" --no-pager > /tmp/kubelet.log"

# GPU metrics and driver errors
ssh core@<node-host> "nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY,UTILIZATION,TEMPERATURE > /tmp/nvidia_q.txt; dmesg | grep -i nvrm -A50 > /tmp/dmesg_nvrm.txt"
```

Sam (Oncall): If we can't access the private VPC from support, ask the customer to run those and upload to our debug-bundles S3 path. Provide a short curl they can run that includes the request-id header so we can correlate.

Maya (Support): I'll send them an ask. What exact curl should I give them to reproduce with request-id header?

Jordan (Infra): Use this (replace host if needed):

```bash
curl -v -X POST "https://api.redwood-inference.internal/v1/generate" \\n  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \\n  -H "X-Request-Id: req_0a1b2c3d4e5f" \\n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \\n  -d '{"model":"redwood/gpt-7b-v1","input":"short test","max_new_tokens":32}'
```

Jordan (Infra): If they can't resolve internal hostname, ask them to add `--resolve api.redwood-inference.internal:443:10.0.5.12` with the cluster's ingress IP to their curl so it hits the private endpoint.

Lina (SRE): Also ask them to run our lightweight tracer that captures tcpdump for 10s around the request. Provide this one-liner:

```bash
sudo timeout 10 tcpdump -w /tmp/acme_capture.pcap port 443 and host 10.0.5.12
```

Lina (SRE): And collect pod resource metrics at time of repro: `kubectl -n acme-corp top pod <pod-name> --containers --no-headers` (cpu/memory).

ops-bot: debug-bundle created: db-20240601-acme-req_0a1b2c3d4e5f (expires in 72h) :package:

Sam (Oncall): Good. Maya, please ask customer to upload these files to the debug bundle S3 path we just created (we'll share presigned URL):
- /tmp/acme_inference_logs.txt
- /tmp/kubelet.log
- /tmp/nvidia_q.txt
- /tmp/dmesg_nvrm.txt
- /tmp/acme_capture.pcap
- output from `kubectl describe pod <pod-name>`
- curl stdout/stderr including `-v`

Maya (Support): Sent to customer with step-by-step. I included the --resolve hint and presigned S3.

Maya (Support): They uploaded a bundle (link) and said the repro curl produced a 500 twice in 6 attempts. I pulled the nvidia output and pasting small snippet: 

```
GPU 0: 90 C, Volatile GPU-Util: 95%, FB Memory Usage: 10.2/11.0 GiB
Persistence Mode: Disabled
Attached GPUs: 1
```

Maya (Support): dmesg shows a couple of driver warnings: `NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79, GPU has fallen off the bus` — customer saw one occurrence at 15:23:11Z.

Jordan (Infra): That Xid 79 is indicative of driver/PCI instability (OOM and GPU reset) — could explain intermittent 500s and timeouts if the inference container loses the device. Next we should check node kernel logs and whether we saw a kubelet pod eviction/restart at that timestamp. Also check our inference runtime logs for `kv-cache` or `session` errors.

Lina (SRE): I'll correlate the pod restart times with `kubectl get events -n acme-corp --field-selector involvedObject.kind=Pod` and filter around 15:20-15:30Z. Also recommend enabling a canary route to lower-replica model variant while we triage.

Sam (Oncall): If it's a hardware issue (GPU resets), ops needs to move workloads off that host and mark for hardware replacement. Lina, can you confirm whether multiple tenants on that node reported issues?

Lina (SRE): Checking now — the bundle has logs from two other tenants with high GPU error rates in the same minute. Looks correlated.

Jordan (Infra): Next actions:
- Ops: quarantine node node-eu-3 and migrate pods (drain)
- Support: notify ACME we're treating as infra hardware fault; offer immediate mitigation (scale up other replicas or move tenant)
- Infra: escalate to colo support for GPU replacement / driver update

Maya (Support): Notified customer, offered mitigation and ETA. They asked for timeline; I gave ~2-4h initial window.

ops-bot: node quarantine initiated: node-eu-3 (started draining) :warning:

Sam (Oncall): I'll follow up with a postmortem template once resolved. Good catch on the Xid.

Maya (Support): Customer confirmed latency improved after we moved one replica to a different node (was able to serve without 500s). They're keeping an eye on it. :thumbsup:

Jordan (Infra): Please attach the debug bundle ID and the key logs to the incident ticket before closing.

Maya (Support): Attached bundle db-20240601-acme-req_0a1b2c3d4e5f and node logs to ticket #INC-4521. Closing thread when infra confirms replacement.

Lina (SRE): Noted. Will update when colo confirms hardware replacement.

Maya (Support): Thanks everyone.
